newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle says gene soybeans pose no problems.
newsitem.headline: Nestle says gene soybeans pose no problems.

text.p: Nestle SA said it was convinced that new, genetically manipulated soybeans from the U.S. posed no problems and that it saw no need to separate them from conventional beans or give them special labels.

"The American and European authorities have looked at these beans very closely and decided to approve them for nutritional use. We see no reason to doubt the reliability of this review," company spokesman Francois Perroud told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We believe these products meet the requirements in every way," he added.
Unlike the European Union, Switzerland has not yet approved the manipulated soybeans, which are being harvested for the first time this year from nearly one million acres in the U.S.
A decision is expected later this year, and Nestle will comply with it, Perroud said.
Separating genetically altered soybeans or requiring them to be labelled was not necessary, he said, adding, "I can hardly imagine how one could formulate such a description."
Swiss retailers Coop and Migros have demanded genetically altered soybeans be separated and labelled.
The environmentalist group Greenpeace has also launched an international protest campaign against the beans, developed by Monsanto Co.

The products, made resistant to a weed-killer, have been declared safe by health authorities in the U.S., Europe and Japan, but Greenpeace says allergic reactions cannot be ruled out and says their impact on the environment remains unknown.
